title: P256 factor base research plan
target: P-256 over its published prime field; comparison curves diagnose specific structural differences.
objective: Identify two factor-base directions worth pursuing beyond the week, with explicit algebra, reproducible code or a precise obstruction, and complete cost accounting.
status: Proposed week of work. Only the starting algebraic identities have been checked in this planning step.
notation: r is the target subgroup order, M the canonical factor-base size, d the decomposition arity and k the composition depth.

tracks.name: Implicit symmetric bases and shifted torus cosets
tracks.question: Can symmetry be applied before membership elimination so that a composed factor base remains implicit throughout relation solving?
tracks.experiment: Use the existing symmetric S4 expression together with the three-variable quadratic map induced by x -> x^2-2. Compare the ramified terminal D_S(x)=2 with generic coset terminals D_S(x)=c, c=Tr(z0^S), and coordinate transforms at matched base cardinality.
tracks.deliverable: An exact symmetric membership circuit, two candidate elimination strategies, certificates of accepted complete solution sets, and operation/memory growth in M and k.
tracks.continue_if: A solver or a defensible cost analysis avoids materializing one dense pair polynomial per base point. Merely having a short circuit is an open lead, not a speed result.
tracks.scope: Direct P-256 work. Constructed positive queries test correctness; rare uniform-target successes are assessed using counting arguments, not a handful of empty runs.
tracks.chat_test: Symmetrize the whole membership problem; try unramified cosets before expanding polynomials.

tracks.name: Auxiliary elliptic curves and isogeny-defined bases
tracks.question: Do rational isogeny maps provide a more useful coordinate domain than the Dickson torus map on the same P-256 field?
tracks.experiment: Start with an auxiliary supersingular curve A: y^2=x^3+x over the P-256 field, whose rational order is p+1. Certify a cyclic power-of-two subgroup and build a low-degree isogeny chain. Use kernels and generic fibres to define x-domains, then lift those coordinates onto the fixed target P-256 curve.
tracks.deliverable: A certified auxiliary curve, a rational-map chain and a matched comparison against F1 using the same M and d.
tracks.continue_if: The resulting relation system has a concrete structural advantage after construction, denominators, rejected coordinates and root solving are charged.
tracks.scope: The auxiliary curve defines coordinates; it is not a replacement target group or a transfer of P-256 into a smooth group.
tracks.chat_test: Replace the torus with a separate auxiliary elliptic curve supplying a rational-map tower.

tracks.name: Coefficient-labelled bases and a single useful relation
tracks.question: Can reducing the number of required useful relations outweigh the cost of constructing and solving over the base?
tracks.experiment: Reproduce the Amadori-Pintore-Sala construction R_i=a_i G+b_i Q and the hybrid/symmetry improvements studied by Kudo et al. Search for one dependency with nonzero net Q coefficient. Compare random labelled bases with structured or adaptive variants whose labelling cost is explicitly known.
tracks.deliverable: A costed single-relation solver formulation, construction ledger, and comparison with rho, BSGS and the many-relation pipeline.
tracks.continue_if: Obtaining labels and useful dependencies changes the total cost; no logarithm oracle is hidden in base construction. Track trivial cancellations and dependencies whose Q coefficient is zero.
tracks.scope: This legitimately changes the rank requirement of the previous pipeline. It does not by itself make random point sets cheaply solvable.
tracks.chat_test: Track a_i G+b_i Q and seek one useful dependency instead of filling a large matrix.

tracks.name: Nonuniform divisor relations and partial-relation stitching
tracks.question: Can carefully chosen curve functions produce more independent useful relations than uniform point decompositions?
tracks.experiment: Use explicit Riemann-Roch spaces and coefficient/interpolation rules with stated sampling distributions. Compare multiple pole orders, anchoring rules and structured bases. Retain equations containing one or two outside-base points, then attempt cycle cancellation to recover full-base relations.
tracks.deliverable: Exact divisor checks, a partial-relation graph, independent-rank growth per total resource cost, and matched conditional-sampling controls.
tracks.continue_if: Any yield improvement survives removal or separate accounting of inverse-pair cancellations, anchors, dependent rows and graph-storage costs.
tracks.scope: An outside-base point is what 'large prime' means here. This extends the earlier function tests by changing the relation mechanism and recycling partial relations.
tracks.chat_test: Generate principal-divisor relations nonuniformly and recycle one or two leftover points.

tracks.name: Isogenous representatives of the target curve
tracks.question: Can a reachable representative of the same target isogeny class support cheaper membership or relation solving?
tracks.experiment: Audit the hypotheses and evaluation costs of the proposed isogeny methods, then screen small-degree maps over F_p. Compare coordinate changes with genuine isogenies and verify subgroup-preserving transport.
tracks.deliverable: A bounded catalogue of reachable models, explicit maps and candidate bases, or a precise construction-cost obstacle.
tracks.continue_if: The destination improves relation cost enough to pay for finding and evaluating the map. Point count, trace and the ordinary CM field stay fixed.
tracks.scope: P-256 itself has no F_p-rational degree-two isogeny; its cubic has no rational root. This is different from the auxiliary-curve isogeny tower in F2.
tracks.chat_test: Search equivalent target representatives, charging discovery and transport.

tracks.name: Interval or digit-box bases with lattice-assisted solving
tracks.question: Can a coordinate box make summation-polynomial roots accessible through a valid small-root argument?
tracks.experiment: Choose explicit interval or digit-box domains. Derive monomial shifts, determinant bounds and integer zero-lifting inequalities before LLL experiments. Check independence or zero-dimensionality wherever the multivariate step is conditional.
tracks.deliverable: A valid parameter window intersecting the required base-size range, or a quantitative explanation of why it does not.
tracks.continue_if: The argument applies to an ordinary public ECDLP instance, without assuming leaked coordinates, hidden small scalars or a univariate theorem for a multivariate system.
tracks.scope: Speculative theory screen. A lattice reduction output alone is not a certified solver or an asymptotic result.
tracks.chat_test: Check whether small-coordinate boxes satisfy actual lattice root-recovery bounds.

tracks.name: Auxiliary covers and compatible branch geometry
tracks.question: Can a cover or correspondence produce a relation space with genuinely better geometry and a costed route back to P-256?
tracks.experiment: Record explicit maps, field, branch orbits, genus, hyperelliptic status and the target subgroup factor. Check Frobenius and ramification constraints before constructing candidate fibre products.
tracks.deliverable: One explicit costed correspondence worth implementing, or a scoped geometric obstruction.
tracks.continue_if: The full destination algorithm and subgroup/field transfer are competitive. Genus alone, or a faster algorithm on a larger ambient Jacobian, is insufficient.
tracks.scope: This revisits an existing SafeCurves lead with stronger applicability tests, rather than declaring it a newly discovered attack.
tracks.chat_test: Screen covers by their maps, field and branch geometry before attempting a solver.

tracks.name: Endomorphism-orbit factor bases
tracks.question: How much do genuine extra automorphisms change unknown counts and relation-solving costs?
tracks.experiment: Use secp256k1 to build automorphism-closed bases and reduce to orbit representatives. Verify the scalar eigenvalue relations and compare against baselines that use the same automorphisms.
tracks.deliverable: An orbit-compressed control and a distinction between constant-factor savings and a changed scaling mechanism.
tracks.continue_if: A proposed P-256 analogue supplies an explicit valid map; the secp256k1 structure is not assumed to transfer to P-256.
tracks.scope: A comparison curve and reusable solver optimization, not the main P-256 claim.
tracks.chat_test: Use secp256k1 as a control for genuine orbit compression.

comparison_set.name: P-224
comparison_set.purpose: Split multiplicative-subgroup construction and comparison with the P-256 nonsplit trace construction.

comparison_set.name: secp256k1
comparison_set.purpose: Real endomorphism-orbit structure; baselines must receive the same symmetry advantage.

comparison_set.name: Curve448
comparison_set.purpose: Another prime field with a large power of two in p+1, including explicit prime-subgroup filtering.

comparison_set.name: Existing F_p^3 construction
comparison_set.purpose: Positive control for implicit membership and certified elimination; it is a changed field and curve, not a P-256 result.

schedule.work: Freeze notation, baselines, seeds and proof/assumption ledger. Audit the single-relation literature. Formalize F1 coset and symmetric membership; prepare F2 auxiliary curve.
Prototype F1 while keeping membership implicit. Record expression/degree growth, solver work and complete-set certificates.
Construct and audit F2 auxiliary isogeny chains and generic fibres over the actual P-256 field. Reuse the F1 solving infrastructure.
Prototype F3 labelled-base dependencies and hybrid solving. Charge construction and require a nonzero target coefficient.
Bounded F4 divisor/partial-relation experiment. Measure useful independent information and account for stitching.
Run targeted P-224, secp256k1 and Curve448 controls. Give F5-F7 bounded mathematical screens, not three extra full implementations.
Independently verify survivors, complete the total-cost and rank/target-attachment accounting, and select at most two follow-on directions.

accounting: Keep base construction, membership solving, point recovery, failed queries, relation stitching, rank, linear algebra and final target attachment in the same cost ledger.
Track complexity in r, M, d and k. Give actual field arithmetic checks and a reasoned model of representation growth; a bounded parameter sweep alone does not establish scaling.
Maintain two explicit scenarios: one target with setup charged, and many targets with reusable setup. Compare the latter with generic fixed-base precomputation, not only fresh brute force.
Use exact membership and point-sum certificates. Distinguish complete solution sets, certified empty sets and runs that ended without a certificate.
Use constructed cases only for correctness. Keep independent targets, generation methods and sampling assumptions separate; no hidden scalar labels reach the search algorithm.
Record rank and nonzero target information, not just raw relation counts. Give identical symmetry, subgroup and amortization advantages to comparators.
Reuse the prior dense-fibre and short-coefficient results as controls. Reopen them only after specifying the new mechanism.
week_end_output: Eight research cards classified as promising, open, or closed for a stated reason; the labels describe evidence rather than enthusiasm.
Implementation/certificate bundles for completed prototypes, with exact proof statements and clearly identified assumptions.
One comparable cost table for the fixed P-256 target and the selected controls.
At most two next directions, each with its remaining mathematical obstacle and next decisive experiment.

sources.title: Petit, Kosters and Messeng, Algebraic approaches for ECDLP over prime fields, PKC 2016
sources.role: Composed rational membership and auxiliary-isogeny factor bases; sections 3.3-3.4.

sources.title: Amadori, Pintore and Sala, On the discrete logarithm problem for prime-field elliptic curves, 2018
sources.role: Coefficient-labelled bases and the single-dependency formulation; section 3.

sources.title: Kudo, Yokota, Takahashi and Yasuda, Acceleration of Index Calculus for Solving ECDLP over Prime Fields and Its Limitation, CANS 2018
sources.role: Hybrid enumeration and symmetry improvements, together with their limitations.

sources.title: Faugere, Gaudry, Huot and Renault, Using Symmetries in the Index Calculus for Elliptic Curves Discrete Logarithm
sources.role: Symmetry techniques developed for extension-field problems; applicability to the proposed prime-field systems must be checked.

sources.title: Galbraith, Climbing and descending tall isogeny volcanos
sources.role: Target-representative isogeny construction; audit exact hypotheses and map-evaluation costs before application.

sources.title: Bernstein and Lange, Safe curves for elliptic-curve cryptography
sources.role: Existing leads concerning curve representatives and auxiliary geometry, with their conditional scope.

sources.title: Diem and Thome, Index calculus in class groups of non-hyperelliptic curves of genus three
sources.role: Geometric distinction relevant to cover screening; no automatic P-256 transfer is assumed.
